stemMd: Which product class commonly forms when a carboxylic acid reacts with an alcohol under suitable acid-catalysed conditions?
explanationMd: Esterification joins the acid-derived acyl portion and the alcohol-derived oxygen-containing portion, commonly releasing water. The product has the –COO– linkage of an ester. The reaction is reversible, so suitable conditions are used to favour product formation.

distractorRationale.c: Organic esterification cannot produce a metal element.
distractorRationale.d: The reaction rearranges chemical bonds without forming a new element.
distractorRationale.a: That does not match the organic reactants and functional-group transformation.
distractorRationale.e: Protein formation requires amino-acid building blocks, not arbitrary acid and alcohol.
